note: 'Sepoy Mutiny first started in' — official key: Barrackpore (Mangal Pandey's outbreak). Mangal Pandey IS taught in this chapter from NIOS Ch. 11 (he hit and wounded a British sergeant; arrested and hanged), but neither fetched source names Barrackpore as the place: NCERT Themes III Theme 11 does not mention Mangal Pandey at all, and the NIOS lesson gives no place. The Barrackpore location could not be verified from an authorised fetched source (NCERT Class VIII 'When People Rebel', hess105.pdf, was unreachable from this machine), so the item is marked untaught and the gap is disclosed in the chapter's outbreak exam_note.

Part of India largely unaffected: Punjab. NCERT Theme 11 (p. 305): the second British force came 'from the Punjab – which was largely peaceful'. Taught in the repression section and q35. (The bank item's 'All of the above' option is not reproduced in the chapter's own questions, per book rules.)

Governor-General at the outbreak: Lord Canning. NCERT Theme 11 (p. 313) names him 'Governor General Canning' in the Clemency of Canning passage; taught in the repression section, its exam_note, people (Canning) and q37. Dalhousie is taught as the predecessor whose annexations caused the revolt — the classic trap is covered.

Leader of Lucknow: Begum Hazrat Mahal (official key). NCERT Theme 11 (p. 299) says the Awadh taluqdars 'joined Begum Hazrat Mahal (the wife of the Nawab) in Lucknow to fight the British'; she is in people. NCERT also says the Lucknow populace hailed her son Birjis Qadr as leader — the leaders section's dont_confuse box teaches both roles so the student can answer the key and understand the distinction.

Kanpur leader: Nana Sahib (NCERT Theme 11, p. 292: sepoys and townspeople gave Nana Sahib 'no choice save to join the revolt as their leader'). Taught in leaders section, people and q20; Tantia Tope handled in an exam_note as the distractor.
Mughal emperor during the revolt: Bahadur Shah II (Bahadur Shah Zafar). NCERT Theme 11 (pp. 288, 292): he agreed to be the nominal leader; taught in outbreak and leaders sections, people and q02/q21.
Symbol circulated by the rebels: chapati. NCERT Theme 11 (pp. 294-295): chapattis distributed village to village, read as an omen of an upheaval. Taught in the rumours section and q08.
Governor-General during the revolt: Lord Canning. Same coverage as WBCS 2017 Q105 (NCERT p. 313 'Governor General Canning'; repression exam_note names both exams' trap, Dalhousie).
